main_text.p: Θεωρέω, contemplor, to stare. Vulgo, ab aftrorum seu stellarum (quæ starres) contemplatione. Ego istud verius credo.

Θρέω, clamo, loquor; Σπόος, fonus, sermo. (hinc ἀλλόσποος, Homero, diverfilinguis:) Angl. I trow, id est, puto, credo. Putare & loqui, affinia natura: Unde אמר Hebraeis, utrumque: & vulgo dicimus, what say you? Lat. Quid ais? sententiam rogantes.
Θρύς, tumultus, clamor; Anglis, a throng, turba, tumultus, vel tumultuosa hominum congeries. Nisi tamen ex Σπρύβω, quod idem; vel, ἀσπόω, confertus.

Θορέω, salio, insilio; Σπρω, impetuosus: qui cum impetu assultat: Anglis, throwes, parturientium dolores, ἀδῖνες, qui subiti & impetuosi esse solent. Sed in genere, throwtigen, pati, Saxonicum. (Matth. XVII. v. 12.)
Θερμός, calidus, warme. Vide in Κεύω.

page.notes: Greek and Hebrew words are transcribed as closely as the scan allows; the Hebrew word in the Anglis entry and some Greek accents are doubtful. Marginal mark "I" at the lower right is a printed or stray character, not text.
